I reviewed the four uncommitted files. The diff converts `AxiosError` and `CanceledError` to ES classes. The main problems are in the rewritten `AxiosError.from`. I only read the diff and grepped the callers, so I haven't run the tests.

- **`lib/core/AxiosError.js:8`, `from()` regressions.**
  - It no longer copies the original error's own properties, so Node fields like `errno`, `syscall`, `address` and `port` are lost.
  - It throws a `TypeError` on a null or undefined `error`. `fetch.js:257` passes `err && err.code`, so `err` can be falsy there.
  - The old default message `'Error'` is gone.
- **`lib/core/AxiosError.js:10`.** `cause` is now enumerable. The old code made it non-enumerable on purpose to avoid JSON noise.
- **`lib/core/AxiosError.js:8`.** `code || error.code` replaces `code == null ? error.code : code`. An explicit falsy code now loses to `error.code`. This is minor, and I'm less sure it matters.
- **`lib/core/AxiosError.js:36`.** `status` is now `undefined` instead of `null` when the response has no status.
- **`lib/core/AxiosError.js:29`.** `isAxiosError` is now an own enumerable property instead of a non-enumerable prototype one. It shows up in spreads, `Object.keys` and equality checks.
- **`lib/cancel/CanceledError.js:18`.** `__CANCEL__` is now an own enumerable instance property instead of a prototype one. The effect is the same as for `isAxiosError`. An object built with `Object.create(CanceledError.prototype)` also stops being recognized by `isCancel`.
- **Tests (`AxiosError.spec.js:53`, `CanceledError.spec.js:15`).** The new `isNativeError` tests use `require` inside ESM specs and skip silently outside Node. Nothing covers the `from()` regressions above.

I found no remaining `AxiosError.call` or `inherits(..., AxiosError)` callers in `lib`, so the class conversion doesn't break any call sites I could find.

input.command: grep -rnE "AxiosError\.call|inherits\(.*AxiosError|CanceledError\.call|AxiosError\.prototype|Object\.create\(.*AxiosError|\.status\b.*null" lib index.d.ts | head -20; grep -rn "from(" lib --include=*.

findings.summary: The rewritten AxiosError.from no longer copies the original error's own properties, and it throws when error is null or undefined.
findings.failure_scenario: The old version used toFlatObject, so errno, syscall, address and port from a Node network error carried over to the AxiosError. Callers in http.js and fetch.js (for example http.js:777 and 817) lose those fields. fetch.js:257 passes `err && err.code`, so err can be falsy. In that case `error.message` throws a TypeError and hides the real failure. The old code defaulted the message to 'Error'.

findings.summary: `cause` is now an enumerable own property. It used to be non-enumerable, which the old comment said was deliberate to avoid JSON noise.
findings.failure_scenario: Object spread, Object.keys, util.inspect, structured logging and serializers like JSON.stringify or structuredClone now include the full original error as `cause`. This adds noise and can expose nested data or cause circular-structure problems.

findings.summary: `code || error.code` replaces the old `code == null ? error.code : code`.
findings.failure_scenario: An explicit falsy code such as '' no longer takes precedence over error.code. This is a minor behavior change.

findings.summary: `this.status = response.status` drops the old `response.status ? response.status : null` normalization.
findings.failure_scenario: A response with a missing or 0 status now gives `error.status === undefined`. Before, it was null. Code or tests that compare against null break.

findings.summary: `isAxiosError` is now an own enumerable instance property. It used to be a non-enumerable prototype property.
findings.failure_scenario: The flag appears in Object.keys, spreads and deep-equality checks, and it gets copied when an error is cloned. For example, `{...err}` or `toEqual` assertions on errors now include isAxiosError: true.

findings.summary: `__CANCEL__` is now an own enumerable instance property. Before, it was non-enumerable on the prototype.
findings.failure_scenario: Serialization and cloning of a CanceledError now expose __CANCEL__. A plain object created with `Object.create(CanceledError.prototype)` is no longer recognized by isCancel.

findings.summary: The new tests use `require('node:util/types')` inside ESM spec files and guard on `process.release.name`.
findings.failure_scenario: In the browser or karma suites `require` can be undefined, or the guard skips the assertion silently, so the test can pass without checking anything. The same pattern is in CanceledError.spec.js. There are also no tests for the AxiosError.from regressions above.
